originalTitle: US stocks today: Nasdaq, S&P fall over 1%, end lower for week as chip selloff broadens
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a bad day, with two important groups of stocks (Nasdaq and S&P) falling by more than 1%. This happened because some technology companies that make computer chips, especially those related to artificial intelligence, saw their stock prices drop sharply. As a result, many investors became cautious and sold their stocks, which made the market fall. Some energy companies, however, saw their stock prices rise because of increasing oil prices due to tensions in the Middle East. Overall, this means that the stock market ended the week on a low note, despite some positive news from banks and other companies.

originalTitle: Reliance Retail Q1 revenue rises, but profit falls as e-commerce weighs
simplifiedContent: Reliance Retail, a big retail company, had an 8.2% increase in sales in the first quarter, which is a good sign. However, the company's profit decreased by 14.2% because it spent a lot on its e-commerce business, which affected its overall margins. This means that even though the company sold more, its investments in online shopping cut into its profit. Reliance Consumer, a part of the company, did very well with its sales more than doubling, especially with its grocery, electronics, and online commerce segments. This mix of increased sales and decreased profit is important for investors to know as it shows both positive and negative trends in the company's performance.

originalTitle: JSW Steel’s profit doubles on revenue growth, beats estimates
simplifiedContent: JSW Steel, a steel company, made a lot of money in the last quarter - its profit went up by more than double compared to the same time last year. The company's revenue, which is the money it makes from selling its products, also increased by about 10% from last year. This increase in revenue, along with lower costs, helped the company make more money. The company's total expenses didn't go up as much as its revenue, which also helped its profits. This is a positive sign for the company, as it was able to do better than expected and is sticking to its plans for spending money on new projects this year.

originalTitle: Netflix shares tumble 13% after weak sales forecast, hit 22-month low
simplifiedContent: Netflix's stock price dropped by 12.6% to its lowest point in 22 months. This happened because the company said it doesn't expect to make as much money as people thought it would, even though its recent results were okay. The company is facing some challenges, including how well its original content is doing and the fact that its stock price has been going down since the middle of 2025. As a result, Netflix is being more cautious about how much money it thinks it will make in 2026. This is why investors are selling their Netflix shares, causing the price to fall.

originalTitle: Sebi clears automatic SWP, STP mandates for demat mutual fund holdings
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market regulator, Sebi, has made a new rule that allows automatic transfers of money from mutual funds held in a demat account. Previously, this was only possible for mutual funds held in a different form. This change means that investors can now set up automatic instructions, such as systematic withdrawal plans (SWP) or systematic transfer plans (STP), for their demat mutual fund holdings. This matters because it gives investors more flexibility and convenience in managing their investments. It also means that investors can now easily transfer money from their demat mutual funds to other accounts or investments on a regular basis.

originalTitle: Pulse of the Street: Earnings sentiment rescues volatile week; real test ahead
simplifiedContent: This week, the Indian stock market had some ups and downs, but it ended on a positive note. The two main stock market indices, called the Sensex and Nifty, both went up - the Sensex by 0.75% and the Nifty by 0.53% for the week. Most of the gains happened on the last day of the week, Friday, when the Nifty jumped 1.1% and the Sensex went up 1.25%. This means that the stock market ended the week at a higher level than where it started. The Sensex even reached its highest closing level since June 12, 2026, which is a significant milestone.
